item.title: Lynette Howell Taylor Re-Elected President of Motion Picture Academy
item.description:
[Intro music fades out]
Host: "Welcome to our show, where we bring you the latest updates from the world of entertainment. Today, we're talking about the Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences, the organization behind the Oscars. The Academy has just announced its new officer positions for the 2026-2027 term, and we've got the details.
Lynette Howell Taylor, an Oscar-nominated producer, has been re-elected as president of the Academy for her second term. She's joined by a talented team of officers, including Lesley Barber, David Dinerstein, Jennifer Fox, Lou Diamond Phillips, and Howard A. Rodman.
These officers bring a wealth of experience to the table. Lynette Howell Taylor produced the Oscar-nominated film 'A Star Is Born', while Jennifer Fox produced 'Michael Clayton'. David Dinerstein won an Oscar for his work on 'Summer of Soul'. And Lou Diamond Phillips, an actor, will be chairing the Equity and Inclusion Committee.
The Academy's CEO, Bill Kramer, expressed his gratitude to the officers for their commitment to the organization and the film community. With the Academy approaching its 100th anniversary, Kramer is excited to continue the vital work of supporting members, the industry, and the Academy's mission.
That's all for today. To learn more about the Academy's new board of governors, you can visit their website. Thanks for tuning in, and we'll see you next time!"
[Outro music starts playing]
